Privacy.title: Privacy Policy
Privacy.intro: Mystonie lets you make artwork for the shows and movies you finish. We collect as little as we can. This page explains what we collect, why, and what you can do about it.

who.title: Who we are
who.body: Mystonie is run by an independent developer (<operator>codenat.me</operator>), who is the data controller for the information described here. Contact: <mail>{email}</mail>.

cards.title: Cards you make
cards.body: Cards are made entirely in your browser. The title you pick, your rating, your review and the date stay on your device and are not sent to us. When you share a card, it goes wherever you send it, under that app's own terms.

account.title: Your account
account.body: If you create an account, we store your email address, a username (made from your name or email; you can change it), the language and time zone you signed up with, and, if you sign in with a social account (Google, Apple, Facebook, X or Discord), the name and profile picture it shares with us. Profile photo: we keep a copy of that picture, or a photo you upload in Settings, in our storage, cropped and resized to 320 pixels; you can change or remove it in Settings at any time, and it is deleted with your account. Sign-in happens through Supabase Auth: we never see or store a password, and each sign-in code is emailed to you and works once. We use this to run your account and to send you sign-in codes. Your page: while your collection is public (the default), anyone with its link can see your display name, username, profile picture, bio, the cards you shared, your collection totals and what you're watching. You can make it private in Settings; cards you shared stay viewable by their link. A card shows your username and profile photo unless you hide them on it. Totals across everyone include private collections, but never who: how many people finished a title (and what share of everyone on Mystonie had finished it when you did) and what's trending on Mystonie, which lists a title only once at least 3 people logged it that week. The same goes for how many people are in a fandom club or joined a monthly challenge, and what a club's members are on lately. While your collection is public, the clubs you joined and the challenges you completed show on your page, and your finishes of titles that fit a club you joined show on that club's page. While you're signed in, a small cookie remembers your chosen language and theme, and it's removed when you sign out. You can download all your data as a file in Settings (Export my data), and your collection as spreadsheets that import back into Mystonie (Export as CSV). You can delete your account at any time in Settings, which immediately removes your profile and everything you've logged.

collect.title: What we collect
collect.body: Waitlist: if you join, we store your email address, the language you used, where you signed up from (for example, from a shared card link) and the time you agreed to be emailed. Searches: the text you type is sent to our server and to the catalogs (TMDB, Google Books, AniList, RAWG) to find titles; we don't store it with anything that identifies you. Imports: an export you import from another app (Letterboxd, Goodreads, MyAnimeList, TV Time) is read on your device. Only the names, years, authors, ISBNs and catalog ids needed to find your titles are sent to our server and the catalogs (TMDB, Google Books, AniList, RAWG), and only what you confirm is saved to your collection. Offline use: so the app works without a connection, the pages you open in it, the posters on them and the titles you looked at lately are kept in your browser's storage on your device, with changes you make while offline until they reach us. Signing out deletes them from the device. Reports: if you report a page or card, we store the reason, your note and, if you're signed in, your account id, and use them only to review the report. Problem reports: if you use Report a problem, we store your message, the page you sent it from, your browser's name and version and, if you're signed in, your account id, and email them to ourselves. We use them only to fix and improve Mystonie and to reply to you, and delete them with your account. Notifications: if you turn on weekly recap notifications in the installed app, we store that device's push address and encryption keys, and delete them when you turn notifications off, sign out, or the device stops accepting them. Abuse protection: to stop automated abuse we count requests per visitor using a one-way, salted hash of your IP address. We never store the IP address itself, and these counters are deleted within a day. Usage and errors: we measure how the site is used (for example, how many cards are made or shared) and collect error reports, without advertising cookies and without building profiles across other sites. Content warnings: if you choose topics to avoid, we store them with your account and only you can see them. Titles are looked up on DoesTheDogDie from our server, never with anything that identifies you. Scene warnings and the warnings quiz: the warnings you add, your votes on them and your quiz answers are stored with your account. Others see the warnings and the totals, never who added or voted. If you delete your account, the warnings you added stay, without your name. Reel of the Day: signed in, your guesses and results are stored with your account (for your streak and stats) and only you can see them; signed out, they stay in your browser. The Journal: signed in, the articles you Stamp or save are stored with your account. Only you see which ones; everyone sees how many Stamps an article has, never who gave them. Tips: if you tip through Buy Me a Coffee, it tells us the email you paid with. If a Mystonie account uses that email, we give it the Supporter sticker; we don't keep the email or anything else about the tip.

use.title: How we use it
use.body: We use your account data to provide Mystonie to you (performing our agreement with you). We use a waitlist email only to tell you when the Mystonie app launches and about closely related product news, and we'll ask before anything else. The legal basis for waitlist email is your consent, which you can withdraw at any time. We use request counters and error reports to keep the service working and safe (our legitimate interest). We don't sell or rent personal information, and we don't use it for advertising.

processors.title: Services we rely on
processors.body: Vercel (hosting), Supabase (database and sign-in), PostHog (privacy-friendly analytics), Sentry (error reports) and Resend (email delivery) process data on our behalf under their data processing terms. Posters and title information come from TMDB (movies and series), AniList (manga), Google Books (books, through our server) and RAWG (games): your browser loads posters, photos of cast and crew, and game art directly from TMDB's, AniList's and RAWG's servers, which see your IP address like any website you visit. If you sign in with Google, Apple, Facebook, X or Discord, that company confirms who you are under its own privacy policy; we ask it only for your name, email address and profile picture (Apple lets you hide your email behind an address it forwards). Notifications you turn on are delivered by your device's push service (Apple, Google, Mozilla or Microsoft); they are encrypted so only your device can read them.

transfers.title: Where data is stored
transfers.body: These services may store and process data in the United States and other countries. Where required, transfers rely on safeguards such as the EU Standard Contractual Clauses.

retention.title: How long we keep it
retention.body: Account data is kept until you delete your account (Settings → Delete account), which removes it straight away. Waitlist emails are kept until you unsubscribe or ask us to delete them, or until we stop the waitlist; deleting your account removes a waitlist entry with the same email too. Every marketing email we send has an unsubscribe link. Request counters are deleted within a day. Analytics and error data are kept for a limited period set in those services.

rights.title: Your rights
rights.body: Depending on where you live (for example under the GDPR, the UK GDPR, the CCPA or Thailand's PDPA), you can ask to access, correct, delete or export your data, object to or restrict its use, and withdraw consent. Email <mail>{email}</mail> and we'll reply within 30 days. You can also complain to your local data protection authority.

children.title: Children
children.body: Mystonie isn't meant for children under 13. You must be at least 13 (or 16 where local law requires) to create an account or join the waitlist. If you think a child has signed up, contact us and we'll delete it.

changes.title: Changes
changes.body: If we change this policy we'll update the date above, and for significant changes to how we use your email we'll tell people on the waitlist first.

Terms.title: Terms of Use
Terms.intro: These terms apply when you use Mystonie. By using the site, you agree to them.

service.title: The service
service.body: Mystonie is a free tool for making shareable artwork about the shows and movies you finish. It is offered as is, it may change, and it may be unavailable at times.

content.title: Your content
content.body: You're responsible for the ratings and reviews you put on your cards and where you share them. Don't use Mystonie to make content that is illegal, harassing, hateful or that infringes someone else's rights. We may remove content or accounts that break these rules.

tmdb.title: Titles and posters
tmdb.body: Title information and posters come from <tmdb>TMDB</tmdb>. This product uses the TMDB API but is not endorsed or certified by TMDB. Game information and art come from <rawg>RAWG</rawg>. Posters and titles belong to their owners; cards are meant for personal, non-commercial sharing.

use.title: Fair use of the site
use.body: Don't scrape the site, send automated requests, try to get around rate limits, or interfere with the service. We may block traffic that does.

brand.title: Mystonie
brand.body: The Mystonie name, logo, mascot and card designs belong to us. You may share cards you made with them as they are.

tips.title: Tips
tips.body: You can tip the maker through <bmc>Buy Me a Coffee</bmc>. A tip is a voluntary gift, paid to and handled by Buy Me a Coffee under its own terms. It doesn't unlock features. If you tip with the email of your Mystonie account, the account gets the Supporter sticker.

liability.title: No warranty
liability.body: To the extent the law allows, Mystonie is provided without warranties, and we're not liable for indirect or consequential losses from using it. Nothing here limits rights you have under consumer laws that can't be waived.

changes.title: Changes
changes.body: We may update these terms. We'll change the date above, and continuing to use the site means you accept the new version.

contact.title: Contact
contact.body: Questions: <mail>{email}</mail>. To report abuse, use Report on the profile or card, or email the same address.

Import.title: Import your history
Import.intro: Bring over what you've watched and read in another app: finishes with their dates and ratings, what you're in the middle of, and what you want to see next.

letterboxd.name: Letterboxd
letterboxd.how1: On letterboxd.com, open Settings, then Data, and choose Export your data.
letterboxd.how2: Pick the ZIP file here as it is (no need to unzip it), or the CSV files from inside it.
letterboxd.brings: Films you've watched with the date and your rating, plus your watchlist.

goodreads.name: Goodreads
goodreads.how1: On goodreads.com, open My Books, then Import and export (under Tools), and choose Export Library.
goodreads.how2: When it's ready, download goodreads_library_export.csv and pick it here.
goodreads.brings: Books you've read with the date and your rating, what you're reading, and your to-read shelf.

mal.name: MyAnimeList
mal.how1: On myanimelist.net, open Settings, then Export (myanimelist.net/panel.php?go=export), and export your anime list, your manga list, or both.
mal.how2: Pick the downloaded .xml.gz files here as they are (no need to unzip them).
mal.brings: Anime and manga you've completed with the date and your score, what you're watching or reading, and your plan-to lists. Dropped titles stay behind.

tvtime.name: TV Time
tvtime.how1: TV Time closed in July 2026. If you downloaded your data before then (its GDPR export), find that ZIP file.
tvtime.how2: Pick the ZIP here as it is. Only your shows, episodes and movies are read: the account and device files inside it are never opened.
tvtime.brings: Every episode you checked in, with its date, the movies you watched, and the shows you followed.

mystonie.name: Mystonie
mystonie.how1: In Settings, under Your data, choose Export as CSV (this account or another one).
mystonie.how2: Pick the ZIP here as it is, or the CSV files from inside it.
mystonie.brings: Your whole collection back: statuses, finish times, ratings, reviews, episodes and reading progress.
